note: post-run review of the ticket test: two finders (numbers and protocol, interpretation), then one refuting check per finding

findings.title: Rules 1 and 3 failed because of which wording each question drew, not because the ticket rule missed its target
findings.evidence: I recomputed every action-item score with own_score. v9's meeting-notes failure only happens when the wording contains the word 'meeting' (writers 1 and 3), and then only on the same 5 data items (-020, -028, -029, -035, -040). Writer 2's wording has no 'meeting', and there v9 already answers from the trackers: v9 = v11 on all 10 action items. The per-question coin flip gave writer 1's wording to 4 of the 10 drawn action items (-020, -021, -029, -035), and 3 of those are failing items. So v11 differs from v9 on exactly 3 of the 50 test answers: -020 0->1.0, -029 0->0.4, -035 0->0.667. That is +2.067/10 = +0.207. On those 3, v11's plan moved from fireflies (action_owner_of / redwood_attendees_of) to 'assignee_of [ticket]', so the targeted switch worked 3 of 3. It also worked 5 of 5 in writer 1 alone (+0.347) and 5 of 5 in writer 3 alone (+0.5). I enumerated all 1,024 equally likely writer-1/writer-2 draws over the 10 action items: only 15.6% reach +0.25.
findings.impact: Under the pre-registration 'not met' is the correct verdict, and nothing justifies changing it. It should be read as 'the drawn set held only 3 instances of the failure the rule targets', not 'the rule fixed too little of what it targets'. The 10 action items are effectively 2 templates over 7 owners, with 3 pairs sharing an owner and expected keys (-014/-035, -020/-028, -029/-040). The +0.207, the 0.912->0.942 headline and the rule-1 verdict all rest on 3 questions and are draw-sensitive. The write-up should say so.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this by re-scoring every answer with own_score, reading the wording-draw code and enumerating the draws. Every number in the finding reproduced.

(1) Writer 2's wording does not contain "meeting". Writers 1 and 3 do, and engine.SYSTEM_WORDS maps "meeting" to fireflies. v9 fails only in writers 1 and 3, and always on the same 5 items: -020, -028, -029, -035 and -040. In writer 2, v9 plans assignee_of on all 10, and v9 equals v11 on all 10.

(2) The draw is rng.choice([w1, w2]) for each question. It gave writer 1's wording to -020, -021, -029 and -035; the other 6 got writer 2's.

(3) In mdtick, the v9 and v11 answer strings differ on exactly 3 of the 50 questions: -020 (0 to 1.0), -029 (0 to 0.4) and -035 (0 to 0.667). That is +2.067/10 = +0.207. v10 against v12 differs on the same 3, and mdtickchanged is the same.

(4) On those 3, v9's plan went to fireflies (action_owner_of, or redwood_attendees_of on -029). v11's plan uses assignee_of [ticket]. The same switch happens on all 5 failing items in writer 1 alone (+0.347) and writer 3 alone (+0.5).

(5) Enumerating the 1,024 writer-1/writer-2 assignments over these 10 items, 160 reach +0.25 (15.6%). The mean gain is +0.173 and the maximum is +0.347.

(6) There are 7 owners. Three pairs share an owner and the expected keys: -014/-035, -020/-028 and -029/-040.

(7) The 0.912 to 0.942 headline comes entirely from these 3 questions. Combine goes from 0.736 to 0.826 because 2.067/23 = 0.090, which is +0.030 on the three-group mean.

One part overstates. The title's "because of the draw, not because the rule missed its target" makes it one cause, and it was two. On the 3 targeted questions, v11 recovered 2.067 of a possible 3.0 points. -029 (0.4) and -035 (0.667) then lost points to the separate due_date→earliest failure, which v9 also makes. With the same draw, fully right answers on those 3 would have given +0.300 and met rule 1. The shortfall needs both the thin draw (3 targets) and the ordering failure.

The verdicts do not change. Rules 1 and 3 are still not met.
verdict.corrected:
No number or verdict changes. The committed raw report needs no edit, but the write-up should state:

"Rules 1 and 3 are not met (v11 − v9 = +0.207 and v12 − v10 = +0.207, against +0.25). Read this result with three points.

1. **The test set held only 3 cases of the targeted failure.** v9's meeting-notes failure needs the word 'meeting' in the question ('meeting' names the meeting-notes system). Writer 2's wording does not contain it. On writer 2's wording, v9 answers all 10 action items from the trackers and v9 = v11. The per-question draw gave writer 1's wording to 4 of the 10 action items, and 3 of those (-020, -029, -035) are items where v9 fails. v11 differs from v9 on exactly these 3 of the 50 answers.

2. **On all 3, the switch worked.** The plan moved from the meeting notes to the assignee's tickets. It also moved on all 5 failing items in writer 1's wording alone (+0.347) and in writer 3's alone (+0.500).

3. **A separate failure capped the gain.** On 2 of the 3 (-029: 0.4, -035: 0.667), v11 then answered the earliest-due key instead of listing every key. v9 makes the same error on other items. The gain was 2.067 of the 3.0 possible. Fully right answers on those 3 would have given +0.300.

Over the 1,024 equally likely writer-1/writer-2 draws for these 10 items, the expected gain is +0.173, the maximum is +0.347, and only 15.6% of draws reach +0.25. So both the +0.207 and the headline 0.912 → 0.942 (combine 0.736 → 0.826) rest on 3 questions and depend on the draw.

The 10 action items cover only 7 owners: three pairs share an owner and the expected keys (-014/-035, -020/-028, -029/-040). The not-met verdict stands as pre-registered. It means: the drawn set held few cases of the targeted failure, and a separate ordering failure capped the gain on 2 of them. It does not mean the switch failed where it applied."

findings.title: All of v11's remaining action-item errors are one-key 'due_date -> earliest' plans, not 'most'
findings.evidence: On the test set, all 8 action items where v11 scores below 1 use the plan '... -> owner -> assignee_of [ticket] -> due_date -> earliest' and return one key. They score 0.667 against 2 expected keys and 0.4 against 4. v9 uses the same plan from the trackers on 6 of these. Writer 3's wording ('Could you please list the keys...') avoids this error: v11 scores 1.0 on all 10 there. Writers 1 and 2 ('which tickets are assigned to them?') both cap v11 at 0.600.
findings.impact: This sharpens 'my reading'. On these 10 questions the ticket rule and the one-key failure are separate effects, and the one-key failure is shared by both arms. It also capped rule 1: 2 of the 3 fixed questions gained only 0.4 or 0.667 instead of 1.0. Without that cap the drawn set would have reached +0.30.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. I recomputed every score with the repo's own measure() and own_score() (cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_multi.py), reading from /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-integratedai/275b943f-979b-5741-9af5-2a07879accea/scratchpad/mdtick, mdtick_w1, mdtick_w2, mdtick_w3 and mdtickchanged.

**Test set (mdtick), v11 on the 10 action items:**
- 020 and 028 score 1.0.
- The other 8 are below 1.0:
  - 014, 021 and 035 return one key out of 2 expected and score 0.667.
  - 027, 029, 036, 040 and 041 return one key out of 4 expected and score 0.4.
- All 8 used a plan ending in "owner -> assignee_of -> due_date -> earliest".
- In every one of the 8, the right answer was sitting in the evidence as an "other plan: ... -> label -> list", with exactly the expected keys.

**v9 on the same 8:**
- On 6 of them (014, 021, 027, 036, 040, 041) v9 used the same tracker plan, "owner -> assignee_of -> due_date -> earliest", and returned the same single key, with the same score.
- On 029 v9 went to the meeting notes (redwood_attendees_of [fireflies]) and scored 0. On 035 it went to the meeting notes (action_owner_of [fireflies]) and scored 0.

**Writers alone:**
- Writer 3 ("Could you please list the keys of the tickets assigned to that person?"): v11 scores 1.0 on all 10, every one by "label -> list".
- Writer 1 ("which tickets are assigned to them? Ticket keys please.") and writer 2 ("...Can you send me the keys?"): v11 scores 0.600 on each, and all 8 of its errors in each are the same one-key plan.
- Writer 3 also has no one-key errors in v9. v9's 5 errors there all come from taking the meeting-notes route.

**Rule 1:**
- The three questions the ticket rule fixed are 020 (0 to 1.0), 029 (0 to 0.4) and 035 (0 to 0.667).
- If 029 and 035 had reached 1.0, v11 would be 0.693 against v9's 0.393, a gain of +0.300.
- Removing the one-key failure from both arms gives the same gain: v9 0.7 and v11 1.0, also +0.300.

**v12 and the changed set:**
- v12 matches v11 on every one of the 10 questions, and the changed set matches the test set. So rule 3 (+0.207) is capped by the same thing.

**One detail in the finding is slightly wrong:**
- Only 7 of the 8 plans carry the "[ticket]" marker.
- 014's v11 plan has no marker: "prepare install runner, hardened profile, and runbook -> owner -> assignee_of -> due_date -> earliest", word for word the same as v9's.

No published number changes. Only the wording of "my reading" needs to change.
verdict.corrected:
Replace "most remaining errors are a different failure both make" with:

"All 8 action items where v11 scores below 1 on the test set use the same plan: 'owner -> assignee_of -> due_date -> earliest'. Seven of the 8 carry the [ticket] marker; 014's plan has none and is the same as v9's. That plan returns the single earliest-due key instead of the list. With 2 keys expected the score is 0.667 (014, 021, 035); with 4 keys expected it is 0.4 (027, 029, 036, 040, 041). In every case the full list was in the evidence as the 'label -> list' alternative.

v9 makes the same one-key choice from the trackers on 6 of these (014, 021, 027, 036, 040, 041), with the same answers and scores. So on these questions the ticket rule and the one-key failure are separate effects, and both arms share the one-key failure.

The wording sets it off. Writers 1 and 2 ('which tickets are assigned to them?' followed by 'Ticket keys please' or 'Can you send me the keys?') each hold v11 to 0.600. Writer 3 ('Could you please list the keys of the tickets assigned to that person?') gets 1.0 on all 10, and v9 makes no one-key errors under that wording either.

This also capped rules 1 and 3. Of the 3 questions the ticket rule fixed, 029 gained only 0.4 and 035 only 0.667; 020 gained the full 1.0. Had 029 and 035 reached 1.0, the gain would have been +0.30 (0.693 against 0.393), and removing the one-key failure from both arms also gives +0.30 (1.0 against 0.7). Both figures are what-ifs: as pre-registered, rules 1 and 3 are not met (+0.207). v12 matches v11 on every one of these questions, and the changed set matches the test set."

findings.title: Rule 3 adds no information: v12 = v11 and v10 = v9 on every answer
findings.evidence: In mdtick, mdtickchanged, mdtick_w1, mdtick_w2 and mdtick_w3, the v10 answers equal v9's and the v12 answers equal v11's on all 50 questions. The form was used for the kind on 4 of 50 test questions (5, 2, 7 and 0 in the other folders) and changed no answer. The forms were made at test time: form_mdtick*.jsonl were born between 21:30:24 and 21:40:28, after the draw at 21:26:43. All 50 entries per file have prompt fingerprint bf3f84a670bd43be and model llama3.2:3b (Ollama digest a80c4f17). The first call took 173 s (cold model load) and the median was 1863.7 ms. The repo copies are byte-identical. The earlier sets' form caches were not touched during the run (mtimes no later than 19:27), so v12 there used only forms cached earlier.
findings.impact: The v12 numbers (0.942; 0.600 on action items) are v11's numbers. Rule 3's 'not met' is rule 1 restated, as the pre-registration expected, and should not be counted as a second result.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute each claim and every one held up.
(1) Answers: in mdtick, mdtickchanged, mdtick_w1, mdtick_w2 and mdtick_w3, v10 equals v9 and v12 equals v11 on 50 of 50 answers in each folder. The plan reasons match too. Only the evidence text differs, in its "other plan" lines.
(2) Kind use: the report counts rows where the form's kind was used because learned_kind was None (factbank_multi.py:799, plans.answer lines 759-761). That gives 4 on mdtick and 5, 2, 7 and 0 on mdtickchanged, w1, w2 and w3. The figures are the same in the v10 and v12 rows.
(3) Timing: the form_mdtick*.jsonl files were born between 21:30:24.3 (mdtick) and 21:40:28.1 (w3). mdtick/questions.jsonl and haystack.json were born at 21:26:43.8.
(4) Model: every file has 50 entries with prompt bf3f84a670bd43be and model llama3.2:3b. Local Ollama has llama3.2:3b at digest a80c4f17acd55265, last modified 2026-09-24.
(5) Speed: the first mdtick entry took 173432.2 ms. The median is 1863.7 ms.
(6) Copies: all five files in cie/docs/benchmarks/factbank_ticket/forms/ are byte-identical to the scratchpad files (cmp).
(7) Earlier sets: their form caches have mtimes of 19:18 or earlier (the latest file in the folder is mdrep_w3 at 19:27). Former only appends on a cache miss, so no new model calls were made for them.
Rule 3's gap (0.600 - 0.393 = +0.207) is therefore exactly rule 1's. The frozen pre-registration (ffdfe2b, line 156) already says "Rule 3 is expected to follow rule 1; it is not a separate confirmation."
One nuance the finding leaves out: the form's fields were also applied, by construction, wherever the form's kind matched the learned kind (43 of 50 on mdtick). They changed no answer there either. Also, v12 = v11 holds only on the five ticket folders. On the earlier sets v10/v12 still differ from v9/v11 on a few questions (mdwords: 45 of 50 equal), while v11 = v9 and v12 = v10 on all 50 there except one mdwords answer (v10 vs v12).
verdict.corrected: The write-up should say: "On the test set, its changed copy and each writer's wording alone, v10's answers equal v9's and v12's equal v11's on all 50 questions. The 3B model's form was consulted for the kind of answer only where the bank's lessons were unsure: 4 of 50 test questions (5, 2, 7 and 0 on the changed copy and writers 1-3). Its fields were applied where its kind matched the lessons' kind. Neither changed any answer. So v12's numbers (0.942 overall, 0.600 on the 10 action items) are v11's, and rule 3's 'not met' (+0.207) restates rule 1. As pre-registered, it is not a second result. The forms were made during the test run (21:30-21:42, after the draw at 21:26:43) with prompt bf3f84a670bd43be and llama3.2:3b (manifest a80c4f17...), at a median of 1864 ms per question; the first call took 173 s because the model was loading cold. On the earlier sets, v12 used only forms cached before the run."

findings.title: The Jira half of the rule is untested: the test set contains no Jira documents
findings.evidence: The mdtick bank's sources are fireflies 8, github 8 and linear 34, with no jira. I checked the 7 people asked about (Priya Shah, Maya Patel, Jordan Blake, Priya Desai, Sofia Martinez, Daniel Cho, Tomás Rivera) directly in factbank_v2.sqlite (read-only): every assignee_of item is a Linear document. jira_people's 'with_jira_tickets: []' is therefore correct but trivially true.
findings.impact: The test checks 'ticket means a Linear item' only. 'Or Jira' had no chance to help or harm, for example through Jira items competing with Linear ones. Rule 2's 40 other questions are at ceiling (1.000 for both arms, identical answers), so rule 2 could only have caught regressions from perfect answers. The known limit (a PR question that mentions a ticket) did not show: issue_pr_author scored 1.0 under v11 in every folder.

verdict.reason: I could not refute the finding. All checks were read-only. (1) The test set has no Jira documents. mdtick/haystack.json dsids mapped through index.json give linear 34, fireflies 8, github 8, and the sources table in factbank_v2.sqlite has the same counts. So do mdtickchanged, mdtick_w1, mdtick_w2 and mdtick_w3. Jira is not rare in the corpus (6,118 documents in the index), but this draw (seed 43) contains none. (2) Every assignee_of item for the 7 people asked about is a Linear document: Priya Shah 2, Maya Patel 2, Jordan Blake 2, Priya Desai 4, Sofia Martinez 4, Daniel Cho 4, Tomás Rivera 4. jira_people's 'with_jira_tickets: []' is therefore empty by construction. (3) The expected answers are built from Linear documents only (factbank_multi.py, `lin`/`by_person`, about lines 282-340). Jira items could therefore never have been rewarded, and only their presence could have harmed a score. (4) Rule 2: in all 5 test folders, v9 and v11 give identical answers on the 40 non-action questions, so it sits at ceiling. One correction to the finding's impact: the rule did fire on 21 of those 40 (person_count 7, person_first 6, pr_issue 8). Their plans read 'assignee_of [ticket]' or 'linked_linear [ticket]'. So rule 2 did exercise the ticket filter, but only over Linear items, with no Jira item to keep or compete. (5) issue_pr_author is 4/4 under v11 and v12 in every test folder, and is also all-correct in every earlier set that has the kind (mdtest has none). These questions start from a ticket key ('a PR that references ticket ENG-4822'). The known-limit form ('PR #N, the one that fixes the login issue') was not asked, so the limit was not tested, not merely absent. (6) The Jira half is barely tested in development either. In the earlier sets, Jira documents appear only as the starting key of ticket_link questions: mdtrain 3/48, the 201-question training set 18, mdfresh 1, mdblind 1. The rule is designed to plan these exactly as v9 does, and v9 and v11 answers are identical on all of them. No question anywhere maps a meeting or PR question that says 'ticket' onto a Jira item, or has Jira and Linear items competing. The finding is low severity. It does not change any rule verdict: rules 1 and 3 are not met, and rule 2 is met.
verdict.corrected: Add to the results write-up (docs/FACTBANK_TICKET_RESULTS.md), under limits or the Jira check: "The test set contains no Jira documents. Its 50 sources are Linear 34, GitHub 8 and Fireflies 8, and the same holds for the changed copy and each writer's set. Every ticket assigned to the 7 people asked about is a Linear issue, so the Jira check ('with_jira_tickets: []') is empty by construction, not a finding. The test therefore checks only 'a ticket is a Linear item'. The 'or Jira' half had no chance to help or harm on it. The expected answers count Linear issues only, so a Jira item in an answer could only have cost points. In development, Jira documents appear only as the starting key of ticket_link questions (3 of the first 48 training questions, 18 of the 201, 1 in the retest, 1 in the general-English blind set). The rule plans those exactly as v9 does, and v9 and v11 answer them identically. No question in any set sends a meeting or pull-request question that says 'ticket' to a Jira item, or has Jira and Linear items compete. Rule 2's 40 other questions are at ceiling, with v9 and v11 at 1.000 and identical answers. The ticket filter did act on 21 of them (person_count 7, person_first 6, pr_issue 8), but only over Linear items, so rule 2 could catch only a loss from perfect answers. issue_pr_author scored 1.0 under v11 and v12 in every folder. Those questions start from a ticket key, so the known limit (a PR question that mentions a ticket in passing) was not asked and remains untested."

findings.impact: The results can be taken as produced by the pre-registered procedure. The open questions are about how to read them (findings above), not about whether they are valid.

findings.title: The +0.207 shortfall comes from the 'earliest instead of list' failure, not from the ticket rule. With that failure absent, the gain would be about +0.30 (counterfactual), and the verdict turns on one question
findings.evidence: Question by question on mdtick (v9 / v11, plan end): 014 0.667/0.667, both tracker→due_date→earliest; 020 0/1.0, v9 meeting notes (action_owner_of [fireflies]→earliest), v11 tracker list; 021 0.667/0.667, both tracker earliest; 027 0.4/0.4, both tracker earliest; 028 1/1, both tracker list; 029 0/0.4, v9 meeting notes (redwood_attendees_of [fireflies]→list), v11 tracker earliest; 035 0/0.667, v9 meeting notes (action_owner_of→earliest), v11 tracker earliest; 036, 040 and 041 0.4/0.4, both tracker earliest. The whole gain is 020 (+1.0), 029 (+0.4) and 035 (+0.667), so 2.067/10 = 0.207. The ticket rule moved all 3 meeting-note answers to the trackers, and every key it returned is correct (precision 1). findings.evidence: In 014 the meeting title contains 'GPU Driver'. SYSTEM_WORDS matches substrings, so systems_named gives ['google_drive', 'ticket'] (and google_drive before fireflies in writer 1/3 wording). The target system becomes google_drive, no plan ends there, and the system check is skipped. v11's plan has no [ticket] filter, and in writer 1/3 wording this same accident also kept v9 off the meeting notes. It changes no number on the test set (014 uses writer 2's wording there).
findings.impact: 'v11 answered every action item from the trackers' is true. 'The ticket rule moved every action item to the trackers' is not: the rule changed the system on 3 test questions (5 in w1 and w3). The write-up should use the first wording, and could note the substring match as a known, older limit.

verdict.reason:
I re-ran v9 and v11 in memory with plans.answer. All 40 stored action-item rows in mdtick and mdtick_w1/w2/w3 reproduce exactly. I then re-ran the 014 rows with "drive" removed from SYSTEM_WORDS. The core of the finding holds:
(1) In 014, the meeting title "MedicaCore - Air-gapped On-Prem Deployment & GPU Driver / Artifact Flow Deep Dive" contains "driver". SYSTEM_WORDS is matched as a substring (`w in ql`), so "drive" names google_drive. In the test set and in writer 2's wording (the same text), systems_named gives ['google_drive'] for v9 and ['google_drive', 'ticket'] for v11. In writer 1's and writer 3's wording it gives ['google_drive', 'fireflies', 'ticket'] for v11.
(2) The start's own system is fireflies, so the target is google_drive. 0 of 87 candidate plans are tagged google_drive, so check 2 keeps nothing and is skipped. v11's 014 plan is v9's own plan with no [ticket] filter. In the test set, w1 and w2 that plan is owner → assignee_of → due_date → earliest, answering ENG-48211 (0.667); in w3 it is the full list (1.0).
(3) Without the stray match, v11 gives the same answers with the [ticket] filter, so no test-set number changes. 014 is the only question in the test set, the changed copy or any writer set with a substring-only system hit.
(4) The count of questions where the rule moved the answer off the meeting notes is right: 3 in the test set (020, 029, 035) and 5 each in w1 and w3 (020, 028, 029, 035, 040). On the other test questions v11 kept v9's tracker plan and only added the [ticket] filter.
(5) The headline sentence "v11 answered every action item from the trackers (v9 answered 3 of 10 from the meeting notes)" is true, and so is the matching line in commit 3332206.
Two corrections to the finding:
(a) "In writer 1/3 wording this same accident also kept v9 off the meeting notes" is wrong for writer 1. Without the stray match, v9 in w1 still picks owner → assignee_of (the trackers), with the same answer. It is true only for writer 3. There, v9 without the stray match answers owner → action_owner_of [fireflies] → list, which scores 0.0 instead of its current 1.0.
(b) The finding misses one consequence: the stray match flatters v9 on writer 3. v9's w3 action-item score is 0.5 as run, but would be 0.4 if the rule alone decided. v10 is affected the same way. So w3's v9 → v11 gain is +0.5 as measured and +0.6 without the accident. No pre-registered rule changes, because the rules are judged on the test set, which uses writer 2's wording for 014.
The "drive" entry has been in engine.SYSTEM_WORDS since the first fact-bank commit (8375901), so it is an older limit, not part of v11. I found no earlier doc that records it, so "known" is too strong.
verdict.corrected:
Keep: "v11 answered all 10 action items from the trackers; v9 answered 3 of 10 (020, 029, 035) from the meeting notes." Do not write that the ticket rule moved every action item to the trackers.
Add: "The rule moved those 3. On 6 others, v11 kept v9's tracker plan and only added the ticket filter. On 014 the rule did not act. The meeting title contains 'GPU Driver', and system words are matched as substrings, so 'drive' names Google Drive. Check 2 then targets Google Drive, no plan ends there, and the check is skipped. v11 answers 014 with v9's own plan (owner → assignee_of → due_date → earliest, 0.667). With the stray match removed, v11 gives the same answer with the ticket filter, so no test-set number changes."
Add: "In writer 3's wording, the same match also kept v9 off the meeting notes on 014. Without it, v9 answers from the meeting notes and scores 0 there, so v9's writer-3 action-item score would be 0.4 rather than 0.5. v10 is the same. In writer 1's wording, v9 picks the trackers either way."
Add: "The substring match in SYSTEM_WORDS predates v11 (it has been there since the first fact bank) and was not recorded before. It is an older limit to fix separately."

findings.title: What the write-up should claim and not claim
findings.evidence: Supported by the checks above. CLAIM: rules 1 and 3 not met (+0.207 < +0.25); rules 2 and 4-7 met. The rule moved every meeting-note answer to the trackers (3/3 test, 5/5 w1, 5/5 w3) and every key it returned was correct. It changed no other answer anywhere. The shortfall comes from a second, shared failure (date ordering set off by the glossary 'which ticket'/'ticket key' → 'key'). Counterfactually, without it the gain would be +0.30 on the test set. Only 3 of 10 test questions had the target failure. DO NOT CLAIM: that rule 1 is met 'in substance' or 'per writer'; that the rule raises action items by +0.30 (counterfactual only); that v12's form contributed; that the earlier 'date in the action item' explanation accounts for these errors; any generalisation to Jira, the PR-mentions-ticket case, or words other than ticket/issue.
findings.impact: This keeps the write-up faithful to the frozen protocol and still states clearly that the rule worked on the failure it targeted. The next fix, the glossary 'key' mapping, gets a precise and testable description.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute the finding and could not, except for one sub-claim, which is wrong as worded. Checks were read-only. For the counterfactual I ran the planner in-process on copies of the databases inside the scratchpad, and nothing was written to the repo.

Confirmed:
(1) Rules 1 and 3 are not met. On the 10 action items, v9 = 3.933/10 = 0.393 and v11 = 0.600, a gain of +0.207. v10 and v12 are identical to v9 and v11 on every action item. Rule 2 is met: the other 40 questions are 1.000 in both. Rules 4-7 are met, as the report says.
(2) The target failure, answering from the meeting notes ([fireflies]), occurred on 3 of 10 test questions (020, 029, 035). It occurred on 5 of 10 in w1 and w3 (020, 028, 029, 035, 040) and 0 of 10 in w2. v11 and v12 moved every one of them to assignee_of [ticket], and the changed copy shows the same 3 of 3. Across all sets, no key returned by v9-v12 on an action item was outside the expected set.
(3) The shared date-ordering failure comes from the glossary. Both v9 and v11 use scratchpad/glossary.json. Its entries 'which ticket' and 'ticket key' map to the answer 'ticket key', which adds the word 'key' to the question's words. In v11's lessons, agg_assoc for 'key' is earliest 21 against list 3. I re-ran v9 and v11 in-process and they reproduced every recorded answer exactly. Then I removed only those two glossary entries at inference. Every 'due_date -> earliest' plan became 'label -> list':
  - test set: v9 0.393 -> 0.700, v11 0.600 -> 1.000, so the counterfactual gain is +0.30, as the finding says.
  - w1: v9 0.253 -> 0.5, v11 0.6 -> 1.0.
  - w2: both 0.6 -> 1.0.
  - w3: unchanged. Its wording ('please list the keys of the tickets assigned to that person') matches neither entry, and it had no ordering error.
  The pull toward 'earliest' is not absolute: 020 and 028 list correctly despite 'key'.
(4) The earlier 'date in the action item' explanation does not fit. The one test action item that contains a date (020) is listed correctly by v11. The 8 that are ordered by date contain no date words.
(5) v12's form contributed nothing: v12 - v10 = v11 - v9 on every action item. The Jira check is empty ('with_jira_tickets': []).

Refuted sub-claim: 'It changed no other answer anywhere' holds for v11 against v9. Across the test, changed, writer, training and seven earlier sets, the only answer changes are the meeting-note moves; mdplan has one changed plan with the same answer. It does not hold for v12 against v10. On mdwords, ticket_link-status-041 ('ENG-73005 references another ticket. How far along is that one?') went from 'SUP-291' (0) to 'In Progress' (1). The plan 'ENG-73005 -> status -> single' read the asked-about ticket's own status, which happens to match the linked ticket's. This is the 'right by coincidence' case the pre-registration already disclosed. A write-up saying the rule changed nothing else would contradict both the data and the pre-registration.
